name: Europium-doped lanthanum strontium cuprate
equilibrium_context: Not a three-dimensional superconductor in equilibrium: stripe order and the LTT phase suppress Tc to a few kelvin; no Josephson plasmon down to 10 K
summary: The original case of light-induced superconductivity in cuprates (Fausti 2011). To date not reproduced by a second group.

driven_states.emergent_property: After resonant excitation of the in-plane Cu-O stretching mode, a Josephson plasma edge appears within one to two picoseconds at about 60 cm^-1 in the c-axis THz reflectivity; the imaginary conductivity adopts a 1/omega divergence, i.e. the signature of coherent interlayer transport.

drive.polarization: E parallel to the CuO2 planes

driven_states.caveat: Optical evidence along c only. No transport, no magnetic-field evidence. The absolute change in reflectance is below one percent; extraction of the conductivity presupposes a homogeneously transformed surface layer above unchanged bulk and is therefore model-dependent. Since 2011 no independent reproduction on LESCO. The saturation critique of Dodge et al. addresses methodologically the same class of reconstruction.

threshold.quantity: no sharp threshold fluence; instead a saturation fluence with a maximum of the photosusceptibility at the phonon resonance at 15 micrometers

further_sources: Nicoletti et al., Phys. Rev. B 90, 100503 (2014), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.90.100503
Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. X 14, 011036 (2024), doi:10.1103/PhysRevX.14.011036 (null result in LBCO)
Dodge, Lopez & Sahota, Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 146002 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.146002 (methodological critique)
driven_states.measured_quantity: c-axis THz reflectivity, and the optical conductivity reconstructed from it

gaps: Pulse duration estimated, not specified in the paper.

provenance.notes: Literature search and field extraction by AI agents under the direction of D. Leonforte (independent researcher); every numerical value and citation checked against the cited work and every DOI verified. Not reviewed by a domain expert. Corrections are welcome and are the intended path to improvement.
